evidence.quote: The results show that Nafion alters the chemical environment of pristine Cu catalyst, leading to the formation of Cu2+ species, likely through partial dissolution induced by the acidic nature of the ionomer, followed by coordination of the dissolved copper species with the sulfonic groups of Nafion.

the sulfonic acid (–SO3H) groups generate a locally acidic environment that promotes partial dissolution of Cu, followed by stabilization of the resulting Cu2+ species through coordination with sulfonate (–SO3−) groups within the polymer network.
the enhanced Cu2+ contribution after Nafion deposition supports that the Nafion coating plays the dominant role in driving the changes in the CuNPs oxidation state.
